answers.children: Yes — Field Spaniels are good with children because their affectionate and gentle nature combines with medium size and controlled energy to allow calm play. Their sensitivity means they respond best to kind interactions rather than rough handling, while their loyalty helps them bond closely with family members of all ages. The breed’s history as an agile hunter in dense cover gives them the stamina to keep up with active kids without becoming overwhelmed. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 8/10)
answers.other-pets: Yes — Field Spaniels generally get along with other pets thanks to their sociable and affectionate temperament. Their background as bird flushing and retrieving dogs produces low prey drive towards household companions, although same-sex tension can appear if they are not introduced carefully. Deep loyalty to family extends to accepting other animals that share their home.
answers.exercise: Field Spaniels need one to two hours of vigorous daily exercise. Bred for flushing and retrieving game in dense English cover, their exceptional stamina requires long hikes, runs or mock hunting sessions; without this their boundless energy leads to destructive chewing or digging. Their energetic and loyal nature makes them thrive when given purposeful outdoor activity.
answers.shedding: Yes — Field Spaniels shed moderately with some seasonal increase. Their medium silky coat lacks the dense undercoat of heavier spaniels yet still produces loose hair that clings to furniture and clothing, while the feathering on legs and ears traps debris from fieldwork and requires regular removal to keep the house tidy.
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is hypoallergenic and the Field Spaniel is not one commonly suggested for allergy sufferers. Its medium silky coat still releases dander and sheds hair that carries allergens, so those with sensitivities should spend time around the breed before choosing it as a companion.
answers.training: Yes — Field Spaniels are easy to train when handled with patience and positive methods. Their high intelligence and trainability allow them to pick up commands quickly, yet their sensitivity to harsh tones demands gentle guidance rather than sharp correction; the breed’s original purpose as an agile hunter in dense cover rewards clear direction and consistent routines.
answers.lifespan: Field Spaniels live 12-14 years. Their medium build and athletic proportions restored by crosses with Springer Spaniels support reasonable health robustness, although their sensitive nature and need for steady activity mean that mental and physical outlets help them remain fit throughout their years.
answers.size: Field Spaniels reach 35-50 lb and stand 17-18 in at the shoulder. This compact yet robust medium build, developed for working dense cover, gives them a substantial feel without being cumbersome indoors, allowing an energetic dog that fits comfortably into most family homes while retaining the agility needed for fieldwork.
answers.barking: No — Field Spaniels do not bark a lot. Their history as quiet workers flushing and retrieving birds in English fields encourages alert but restrained vocalisation, so they tend to stay relatively silent unless they have a genuine reason to communicate with their family.
answers.apartment: No — Field Spaniels do not make ideal apartment dogs. Their boundless energy and need for one to two hours of daily vigorous activity, rooted in their role as stamina-driven hunters, make it hard for them to settle indoors without sufficient outlets, often leading to restlessness or anxiety when space and exercise are limited.
answers.first-time: No — Field Spaniels are not the easiest choice for first-time owners. Their deeply loyal yet sensitive temperament and tendency towards separation anxiety demand consistent time, patient training and ample outdoor activity that can overwhelm novices unfamiliar with channelling the breed’s energetic drive and emotional needs.
